changelog: Fixed the backtesting position tool (Long/Short) never checking which side of entry the stop/take-profit belonged on. Confirmed on live: a Short showed Entry 6883.40, SL 6330.28, TP 5305.40 — both below entry, when a Short's stop must be ABOVE entry. Root cause: btFinalizeNewDrawing() took the drag end's raw price as stop_loss verbatim regardless of direction, so dragging a Short DOWN (the natural gesture, same motion as a Long) put the stop below entry — wrong for a Short, and rejected outright by BacktestController::placeOrder()'s own direction check ('For a Short, stop loss must be above entry.'). The live drag preview had the identical defect. Long was never affected.

New drawing creation and the live preview now treat the drag end as the stop DISTANCE, not its side — the stop always lands on the correct side for the tool (below entry for Long, above for Short) regardless of which way the user drags, matching the Long tool's existing (already-correct) behaviour.

btApplyDrag() now clamps the stop and TP handles to the correct side of entry while dragging (a drag past entry stops at a minimum distance rather than crossing to the wrong side), and defensively re-clamps stop/TP when the entry handle itself is dragged. Minimum distance is 0.01% of entry — this app has no real tick-size concept (prices span 0.0044 to 71,968 on this account alone, per CLAUDE.md's v3.14.5 note), so a percentage-of-entry floor was used instead of a fixed absolute tick, scaling correctly across that whole range.

New helper btNormalizePositionSides(tool, settings): mirrors a wrong-side stop/TP across entry, preserving its original distance, and enforces the minimum distance. loadBtDrawings() now runs this on every position_long/position_short drawing on load and saves the repair once if anything changed — this is what fixes the already-broken live Short without any manual data edit. Verified against the exact live values from the bug report: entry 6883.40 / stop 6330.28 mirrors to stop ≈7436.52, TP (already on the correct side) is left untouched.

The red (entry-to-stop) and teal (entry-to-TP) fills already used the same 0.18 alpha — no colour change was needed. The 'pale greyish-red' look reported on the broken Short was the two zones overlapping (both below entry), not an alpha mismatch; once the geometry fix keeps them on opposite sides, the existing fills render solid on their own.
release_notes: Code-only fix to js/backtest-drawings.js. No PHP, no migration. The existing live broken Short self-repairs the next time its session is opened (loadBtDrawings() now runs the repair automatically) — no manual data fix or DB access needed.
